description: Release-age cooldown: npm's is inherited (config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm: minimumReleaseAge=3 days + internalChecksFilter=strict for the npm datasource); non-npm's is the cooldown packageRule below, which lists its datasources and why Docker is not one.

DO NOT restate minimumReleaseAge on a packageRule that matches lockFileMaintenance or pin. That preset deliberately sets it to null for those update types because Renovate cannot age them; a rule here sorts AFTER the preset and would override the carve-out. With minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required (default since Renovate 42) a missing timestamp counts as not-yet-passed, so the branch is never created — silently stopping the daily lockFileMaintenance run that is this repo's only transitive-dep refresh path (ADR-0027 § 2026-08-06 amendment).

The npm-side cooldown for those paths lives in .npmrc (min-release-age=3). Never add minimumReleaseAge where no release timestamp exists: under timestamp-required the update is held forever, listed as Pending Status Checks, which the nightly health check treats as benign.

Current by default (ADR-0027 § 2026-10-29, control 1): no global schedule, non-majors auto-merge on green CI, majors wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard. prHourlyLimit=0, because a burst held back by the hourly limit is listed as Rate-Limited, which the nightly health check (scripts/ci/renovate-health.mjs) reports as red; prConcurrentLimit stays at Renovate's default, so Rate-Limited means 10 open PRs: a real backlog.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Daily. This is the ONLY Renovate mechanism that refreshes transitive npm deps — vulnerability PRs cover direct deps only (https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#osvvulnerabilityalerts). Its branch is listed as Awaiting Schedule outside the window, which the nightly health check exempts by name.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: deploy-asap: what runs is exposed until deployed; merging opens or extends the "Deploy pending" issue (.github/workflows/deploy-pending.yml, ADR-0027 § 2026-10-29).

packageRules.description: MinIO `minio` and `mc` are a frozen, self-hosted copy of the last community images, digest-pinned — no upstream publishes images any more, so there is nothing to track (ADR-0003 § Dep lifecycle health)

Caddy version appears in three places in docker/caddy/Dockerfile (FROM caddy:X-builder, FROM caddy:X, xcaddy build vX), all tracked against the `caddy` Docker image — the two FROM tags via the built-in dockerfile manager, the xcaddy build version via the customManager below — plus docker-compose.http.yml's stock caddy:X-alpine (its own customManager). Group them so one PR advances all of them to the same version together; sharing one datasource is what makes that lockstep hold. The caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin tracks separately (go).

Suppress abandonment-heuristic false positives — release-date heuristic misfires on stable / maintenance-mode libs. Per-dep rationale + per-row verification dates in docs/ops/dep-management.md § Abandonment-flag verdicts. 3 years keeps real abandonment within range while filtering current noise.

Known-broken releases. @cantoo/pdf-lib 2.11.0 ships bare `.json` imports in its ESM standard-fonts build, so Node's loader throws ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING on any import of the package — it crash-loops the app, not just the tests (https://github.com/Projekt-Manager-Org/Projekt-Manager/pull/413). Fixed in 2.11.1 by `with { type: 'json' }`; 2.10.x does not exist. This rule is only half the exclusion: `allowedVersions` governs what Renovate PROPOSES, and npm never sees it, so it cannot keep the version out of a regenerated lockfile. The binding half is the narrowed range in package.json, which is what npm resolves against; this rule stops Renovate replacing that range with one that re-admits 2.11.0. Both are required — see ADR-0027 § 2026-09-17. Entries are permanent: a release that shipped broken stays broken.

Auto-merge all non-major updates (patch, minor, digest, pin, lockfile maintenance) on green CI — grouped clusters included; grouping consolidates PRs, it does not gate the merge (requires repo Settings → General → Pull Requests → Allow auto-merge)

Majors wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard (Pending Approval) and are never auto-merged: a major needs its migration guide read. The rule above opts in only non-major types, so automerge=false restates the exclusion and survives edits to it. Pending Approval is benign to the nightly health check; an approved major PR left open more than 7 days turns it red.

deploy-asap on updates of the runtime images production builds or runs: the fixes they carry reach a host only on deploy, so merging opens or extends the "Deploy pending" issue (.github/workflows/deploy-pending.yml, ADR-0027 § 2026-10-29). Pins are excluded: they change no bytes. A group gets the label when any of its updates matches (labels are combined per branch). docker-compose.http.yml is evaluation-only, and CI's service images never ship.

No digest pins for docker deps a customManager extracts: the regex captures no digest (the `postgresqlN` apk names in Dockerfile.backup, `xcaddy build vX` in docker/caddy/Dockerfile), so config:best-practices' docker:pinDigests has nowhere to write one, and the failed pin errored the whole grouped pin branch every run (#637). A regex that captures a digest (docker-compose.http.yml) still gets digest updates.

Release-age cooldown outside npm, the same 3 days security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm sets for npm: the malicious-publish window. Only datasources whose release timestamps were verified (dry-run 2026-10-30; ADR-0027 § 2026-10-29): github-tags (Actions, digest updates age against the tag's release), github-release-attachments (CLI binaries) and go (the proxy's `Time`). Not docker, not node-version: Docker Hub refuses anonymous tag paging past 1000 tags, so node and postgres carry no timestamp and timestamp-required would hold them forever; .nvmrc shares the node branch with the image, so a cooldown on it alone splits their versions. Never pin or lockFileMaintenance (see the top-level description). Vulnerability PRs skip the cooldown.

The renovate-config-validator image `lint` runs (ci.yml). Weekly: Renovate releases several times a day, and a PR plus a CI run per release buys nothing for a validator. Its branch is listed as Awaiting Schedule between windows, which scripts/ci/renovate-health.mjs exempts by name: keep the groupName in step with AWAITING_EXEMPT there.

Docker host packages (docker/host-versions.txt, ADR-0009): one grouped PR, never auto-merged. The operator tests the PR branch on the VPS and merges only once it passes acceptance (server-setup.md § Upgrading pinned versions); deploy.sh refuses to deploy until a host matches the file, so an auto-merge would block deploys at a time nobody chose. Sorted after the auto-merge and major rules above so it overrides both. Quarterly, in the first week of January, April, July and October: Docker ships a release almost every week, and every bump costs a daemon restart and a key paste per host. updateNotScheduled=false freezes the PR outside the window; inside it, the PR rebases whenever main moves, so the operator merges once the pins file is unchanged since the tested SHA. A closed PR inside the window is recreated: the group has no single version, so its title is not ignorable. prConcurrentLimit=0 exempts its own creation: a full PR limit inside the one-week window would otherwise skip the quarter (the nightly health check reports Rate-Limited, but the window may close before the backlog clears). While open, it still counts against every other rule's limit (the open-PR count is repository-wide): merge it or close it to skip the round. No dashboard approval: acceptance on the VPS is the approval. No minimumReleaseAge: the deb datasource reports no release timestamps, and with timestamp-required a missing timestamp never ages, so the PR would never be created.
prBodyNotes: **Merge only after acceptance on the VPS:** `sudo /opt/projekt-manager/scripts/ops/docker-bump.sh test origin/renovate/docker-host`, then `merge-check` before merging. Procedure, review checklist and revert: [server-setup.md § Upgrading pinned versions](https://github.com/Projekt-Manager-Org/Projekt-Manager/blob/main/docs/ops/server-setup.md#upgrading-pinned-versions). A `containerd.io` minor change is a one-way door: never skip a minor, and a revert takes step 5c.

customManagers.description: Docker host packages pinned in docker/host-versions.txt (ADR-0009), tracked against Docker's own apt repo for the hosts' Ubuntu release. Each non-comment line is `<package>=<apt version>`; the line-start anchor keeps `#` comments out. Grouped and never auto-merged by the `docker-host` packageRule.

Caddy version inside `xcaddy build vN.N.N` in docker/caddy/Dockerfile. Tracks the `caddy` Docker image (not github-releases) so the built version can only advance to a Caddy release that already has a published image — keeping it in lockstep with the FROM caddy:X base tags, which the dockerfile manager bumps from the same datasource. Grouped under groupName 'caddy' above.

The stock caddy image in docker-compose.http.yml. The docker-compose manager skips that service: Renovate's YAML parser leaves the `!reset` tag unresolved, so `build: !reset null` reads as the string "null", and a service with a `build` counts as built locally (lib/modules/manager/docker-compose/extract.ts). Grouped under groupName 'caddy' above.

Go modules in `xcaddy build … --with <module>[/<pkg>]@vX` in docker/caddy/Dockerfile: the caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin, and two modules pinned above Caddy's own requirement — golang.org/x/net (named through its `/http2` package, because xcaddy blank-imports each --with path and the module root has none) and github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4. Without those two, advisories in the edge proxy's dependencies wait for a Caddy release (#637). The plugin tracks release tags, not master: the go datasource carries a release timestamp, so the 3-day cooldown applies to the code that holds the Cloudflare token (git-refs has none). Same lane as the other Caddy inputs: auto-merged on green CI, which does not build Caddy (ci.yml `docker`, accepted gap); the nightly inventory scan does, so a bump that does not compile turns it red within a day, unless a deploy's own `docker compose build caddy` hits it first — loudly, before anything is recreated.

PostgreSQL major in Alpine apk pins (`postgresqlN`, `postgresqlN-client`, `postgresqlN-contrib`) inside Dockerfile.backup. Renovate's Docker manager bumps the `db` image tag in docker-compose/CI but does not see apk package names. Without this regex a server bump leaves the backup client major behind — pg_dump/pg_restore older→newer is the unsupported direction. extractVersion filters Docker tags to integer-only so we track the major line, matching what the apk package name encodes.

CLI binaries installed by download URL + SHA256 verification (OSV-Scanner, actionlint, ripgrep, age), in a workflow step or a composite-action step — `age` lives in `.github/actions/install-age/install-age.sh`, called from `ci.yml`'s `check-shard`, from `e2e.yml` and from the `build-scan-smoke` composite, so the pattern list covers `.github/actions/<name>/*.{yml,yaml,sh}`. Both halves are load-bearing: a composite's procedure belongs in a sibling `.sh` so CI's shellcheck gate covers it (actionlint does not read `action.yml`), which is where `install-age`'s and `start-minio`'s pins sit, and `action.yml` stays in scope because a composite may still hold an inline `run:` block. Keep the pattern list and the scan roots in `scripts/check-renovate-annotations.mjs` in step: the check scans that same file set, so a class it scans but no manager covers is reported as an untracked pin. None fits the github-actions manager — the first two ship only a Docker action or a reusable workflow, the latter two ship no action at all — so without this manager each is a pin with no update path, the failure mode ADR-0027 exists to retire. The github-release-attachments datasource locates the release's checksums asset from the current digest and re-reads it on the next release, so version and SHA256 advance in the SAME PR — a hand-edited checksum is never required. When no checksums asset matches (age ships only Sigsum `.proof` files) it falls back to hashing the release assets directly and matching on the digest, so a checksum-less upstream is still tracked. Driven by an inline `# renovate:` annotation so the dep is declared at the call site rather than inferred from a URL shape. TWO constraints, both silent when violated: (1) `currentValue` MUST be the literal git tag, `v` prefix and all or neither — `v2.3.8` for OSV-Scanner, `15.2.0` for ripgrep, because the digest lookup calls `GET /releases/tags/{currentValue}` verbatim and either an added or a stripped `v` 404s there. Steps must therefore reference the version through the `version` variable exactly once, deriving any unprefixed form (`${version#v}`) — Renovate rewrites the matched span only. (2) The annotation, `version=` and `expected_sha=` must be CONSECUTIVE lines: matchStrings joins them with `\s+`, so an interposed comment drops the pin out of tracking with no error raised anywhere. `scripts/check-renovate-annotations.mjs` is the guard against both.
